title: Cash Bag - SAO++ edition
credit: Circuit after the NorthSec 2025 badge team's Sao_CashBag, github.com/nsec/nsec-badge (MIT). Drawing: SAO++ (CC-BY-SA-4.0)
notes: SAO++ power select: the switch common feeds the LEDs. Position 1 = badge 3.3 V, position 2 = OFF (pin 2 unconnected), position 3 = coin cell.
The badge supply and the coin cell sit on separate switch contacts and are never connected to each other.
LED-only board: SDA, SCL, GPIO1 and GPIO2 are not connected, so no series diode is needed on the cell (see docs/standard.md section 3).
D1 (the sack's gathered top), D2 (the bank note's medallion), D3 (a glint on the coin): reverse-mount white LEDs on the back, shining through the board.
1.3 k each: about 0.45 mA per LED on badge power, about 0.2 mA on a fresh cell (calculated, not measured). The maker used 330 ohm on 3.3 V.
